title: Microsoft Teams
intro: Independent Year 7 Catch Up based on Lesson 003: Microsoft Teams, assignments, Shared files and Class Notebook.

stages.label: Do Now
stages.lead: Recall what you learned about school email and keeping accounts safe.

questions.prompt: Can school email be used for personal messages?
questions.answer: No — it is for school purposes.
questions.feedback: Use your school email for school work and approved school communication.
options: No — it is for school purposes.

questions.prompt: Name the four main parts of a formal email.
questions.feedback: An appropriate email has a subject, greeting, message body and sign-off.

questions.prompt: Give two ways to make a strong school password.
questions.answer: Use a long password and avoid obvious personal information.
questions.feedback: Follow school password rules; use sufficient length and avoid easily guessed personal details.
options: Share the same password with friends.
Use a long password and avoid obvious personal information.

questions.prompt: Why might someone use Bcc when emailing several families?
questions.answer: It hides recipients' addresses from one another.
questions.feedback: Bcc protects privacy because recipients cannot see other recipients' email addresses.
options: It hides recipients' addresses from one another.

stages.label: I Do
stages.lead: See how a class Team and assignments work.

blocks.title: What is Microsoft Teams?
blocks.text: A class Team helps pupils and teachers communicate, collaborate and find learning resources. Assignments are tasks set for you to complete and submit.

blocks.title: The six-step assignment journey
blocks.text: 1. Sign in using your school account. 2. Open the correct class Team. 3. Find Assignments. 4. Read and complete the task. 5. Choose Hand In. 6. Check the submission status. Opening an assignment alone does not submit it.

blocks.title: Where to look
blocks.text: Shared contains files provided to your class. Class Notebook, powered by OneNote, stores lesson notes and work. Assignments holds tasks for submitting.

questions.prompt: What does a class Team help you do?
questions.answer: Communicate, collaborate and find learning resources.
questions.feedback: A class Team is a shared space for communication and class resources.
options: Communicate, collaborate and find learning resources.

questions.prompt: After completing an assignment, which action submits it?
questions.feedback: In Teams, select Hand In to submit your completed task.

questions.prompt: Where would you find files shared with the class?
questions.feedback: Shared contains class files; Class Notebook stores notes and Assignments handles tasks.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: To submit work: sign in → class Team → Assignments → complete task → Hand In → check submitted. Be careful: completed is not always submitted.

questions.prompt: You have opened a task but have not submitted it. Which step is missing?
questions.feedback: Completing or viewing a task is not the same as handing it in.

questions.prompt: Where should your lesson notes normally be stored?
questions.feedback: OneNote Class Notebook is used for lesson notes and work.

questions.prompt: What should you do immediately after choosing Hand In?
questions.answer: Check that the submission status confirms it.
questions.feedback: Check that Teams shows the assignment has been submitted.
options: Check that the submission status confirms it.

questions.prompt: Where do you find the teacher's task to submit?
questions.feedback: Assignments is for tasks set by the teacher.

stages.label: You Do
stages.lead: Work independently, then reflect on your answer.

blocks.title: Independent scenario
blocks.text: You completed a document in Teams but your teacher says it was not submitted. Think through what may have happened before answering.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely missing action?
questions.answer: You did not choose Hand In.
questions.feedback: You must press Hand In and verify the submission; simply saving is not enough.
options: You did not choose Hand In.
Your document had too many words.

questions.prompt: Which area is mainly for notes rather than submitting assignments?
questions.feedback: Class Notebook holds learning notes. Assignments handles task submissions.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you cannot find your teacher's task?
questions.answer: Check the correct class Team and Assignments, then ask the teacher.
questions.feedback: Use the correct class Team and Assignments tab; ask for help if still missing.
options: Send it using a stranger's account.
Check the correct class Team and Assignments, then ask the teacher.

writing.prompt: Explain the steps you would take to find, complete and correctly hand in a Computing assignment in Microsoft Teams.
writing.model: I would sign in using my school account, open the correct class Team and find the task under Assignments. I would read the instructions and complete my work. I would select Hand In, then check that Teams shows my work as submitted.
checklist: I named the correct class Team and Assignments.
I explained that I must complete my work and choose Hand In.
I said I would check that it was submitted.

questions.prompt: Opening an assignment automatically hands it in.
questions.feedback: False. You must choose Hand In and check its submission status.

questions.prompt: Shared files and Class Notebook serve different purposes.
questions.feedback: True. Shared provides class files; Class Notebook stores lesson notes and work.

questions.prompt: You should confirm that Teams shows your work has been submitted.
questions.feedback: True. Checking the submitted status is the final step.
